images.prompt: A diagram illustrating an arbitrage opportunity in currency exchange. Three circles represent "Starting USD", "Bank A (USD to EUR)", and "Bank B (EUR to USD)". Arrows show the flow: "Starting USD" -> "Bank A" (e.g., $1000 -> 900 EUR), then "Bank A" -> "Bank B" (900 EUR -> $1035), and finally "Bank B" -> "Ending USD" ($1035). The profit of $35 is highlighted as the difference between ending and starting USD, emphasizing the risk-free gain.

images.prompt: A conceptual diagram comparing "Real World" vs. "Risk-Neutral World" for asset pricing. On the "Real World" side, show an asset's expected return being higher than the risk-free rate due to a "Risk Premium". On the "Risk-Neutral World" side, show the asset's expected return being equal to the "Risk-Free Rate", with a note that "Risk-Neutral Probabilities" are used to adjust for risk aversion, effectively embedding the risk premium into the probabilities rather than the discount rate.
